not_covered: New initial orientations, weakened actuators, terrain or impacts
Robot self-collision response or continuous-time path clearance
qualification_economy: Reuse the native owner, compact capture, full reader and retained-path screen. Twenty-four new controls exercise bounded force requests, staged support, prepared response, unchanged command protection, atomic state and factored breadth. Existing exchange controls preserve comparators. No new native runner or reader.
purpose: Search twelve support-sharing recipes across 24 exposed bodies in 192 fresh twelve-second worlds.
selection_rationale: Twelve recipes cross three limb relations, two torque-reserve target weights and two load/unload ramps. Each of 24 bodies receives four recipes, two per ramp and score weight, and at least one per limb relation. Each recipe covers four bodies in each geometric stratum. Fifty concrete profiles include 32 sharing variants, eight selected references, eight exposed failed exchanges and two baselines. Every body receives four fresh comparators. Failed exchange selection uses prior mean reference gain within each reference group; it is exposed design input, not training or held-out selection. Factor assignments are finite screening, not independent population-wide effect estimates.
braking_model_limit: Constant-velocity lookahead and a stopping-speed envelope using a declared 6 rad/s^2 shaping estimate. This is not a validated physical deceleration bound or a guarantee that no joint crosses its limit.
body_moment_limit: Clear geometric targets are not collision-free transitions. Geometric capsule low points are not measured contact locations. Friction cones and normal load are configured proposals; static joint compensation omits inertial, Coriolis, passive and limit forces. Actual force, contact and sampled work are retained. Motors, native collision filtering and eligibility remain unchanged.
code_path_risks_covered: Exact selected reference until measured plateau
Torque-bounded nine-knee-sample and analytic-hip target search with endpoint clearance
Original support request kept while replacement request ramps under existing speed, slew and joint protection
Six measured contact observations and sustained prepared motor response before unloading
Response loss restores old request; release requires previously committed zero old request
Contact loss, unavailable force intervals and phase timeouts restore reference with cooldown
Full replay and same-run compact projection on one exposed route body
Synthetic complete transfer, rollback, upright reset and atomic batch refusal
Prospectively required retained-sample path screening before broad lead promotion
route_horizon_rationale: Six seconds covers reference acquisition, a plateau, up to 180 seek steps, six contact observations and 24- or 60-step loading/unloading ramps. Twelve roles include four fresh comparators and eight variants spanning all limb relations, both target weights and both ramp durations. Supported seeking, contact acquisition, loading, positive staged unloading and bounded fallback must all occur. Complete transfer and rollback have synthetic controls; successful righting is not a route criterion. Missing coverage consumes the route and blocks compact search.
support_sharing_limit: Static force intervals and prepared motor-response checks use a rigid-tree model, measured canonical state and prior commands. They do not measure ground reaction or prove dynamic feasibility. Guarded weights may differ from scheduled weights; both are retained. Pose clearance is endpoint-only and broad leads require retained-path screening. Nominal motor caps, speed/slew limits, joint guards, five-degree gain and recovery eligibility are unchanged.
